/-- Run of H44 (§71, §76–§78; HandlePool v0.5, D.1–D.3): frame 1 with the arena value 0,
the allocator 1, the pool value 2 and the handle leaves 3 and 4; storage 5 owned by 0, with the
place 6 holding the nodes 7 (fields 8, 9) and 10 (fields 11, 12); arena on 5 (`internal` 5); the
block 6 over the leaves of 6 issued to the pool value; pool on 6 with the block as `internal`;
each node resolved in turn, its link field written, then unresolved; `endUse` of the pool value;
`reset` of the arena. -/
def h44o : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 5, pt 6, pt 7, pt 7, pt 6, pt 10, pt 10], .write 0 [0], .newArena 5 5,
  .issue 0 [8, 9, 11, 12] 2, .newPool 6 6, .allocSlot 0 3, .allocSlot 0 4,
  .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify, .write 8 [8, 9], .unresolve 7,
  .resolve 0 ⟨0, 1, 0⟩ .modify, .write 10 [11, 12], .unresolve 9, .endUse 2, .reset 0]

/-- **H44** (material §1 G, class Lib). A cyclic graph whose nodes live in a pool placed on an arena
block, linked by handles; temporary resolutions; end of the resolutions, then of the pool value,
then `reset` of the arena, without following the cyclic links. Expected (material): `ok`.
Obtained: `ok` at every step (§89, §37, §78.2; HandlePool v0.5, D.1: the block region was never
written, so `newPool` finds `Uninit` storage). -/
theorem H44 : CRuns K0 [] h44o :=
  crunsTo (by decide)

/-! ## Handle-pool contract (HandlePool v0.5) -/

/-- State after the first nine steps of `h44o`: the pool on the arena block, both slots allocated,
nothing resolved (§57). -/
def fdi : CState := cfinal K0 [] (h44o.take 9)

/-- **pool_freeSlot_derived_internal** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). `freeSlot` on a pool
whose `internal` is a derived authority (the arena block 6) held by the pool value, outside the
slot. Expected (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors
`internal` et ses ancêtres"; "Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe";
HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1': only strict descendants of `internal` block): `ok`. Obtained: `ok` (the
entry was never written and no active strict descendant of `internal` 6 covers it).

The kernel `endUse` of the slot place 7 on the same state. Historical verdict: `reject` (spec v0
§69.2: `internal` 6, active, derived, covering the slot, is held outside it; the exemption of
`internal` then decided the `freeSlot` verdict of the v0.4 annex, whose `freeSlot` ended the
content). New verdict: `ok` (v0.1 §69.2, the exemption of the authority on which the `Modify`
right over the place rests and of its origin chain: that right over the place 7 rests on 6).
Obtained: `ok` (`EndUsePre`). Under HandlePool v0.5 `freeSlot` has no end-of-use effect (HP5-1),
so the two verdicts no longer depend on each other. -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_derived_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (h44o.take 9) fdi ∧
    EndUsePre K0 fdi.kern 7 ∧ CRuns K0 [] (h44o.take 9 ++ [.freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), by decide, crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **resolveMany_observe_repeat** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). `resolveMany` in
`Observe` of a repeated valid handle. Expected (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "sans `split` ni
contrôle de distinction : la répétition du même handle valide est permise"): `ok`. Obtained: `ok`
(one `Observe` companion, two `Observe` entry authorities derived from it, §60). The same batch in
`Modify` is `fail` (`H31b`). -/
theorem resolveMany_observe_repeat :
    CRuns K0 [] (h31bo ++ [.resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe]) :=
  crunsTo (by decide)

/-- **resolveMany_atomic** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). `resolveMany Modify` of a batch with
one valid handle and one stale handle. Expected (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "`fail` atomique, sans
création partielle de droits"; HP5-5): `fail`. Obtained: `fail`, and `fail` is the only outcome of
the relation (no authority is created, §58). Twin without the stale handle (the two valid
handles): `ok`. -/
theorem resolveMany_atomic :
    HandlePool.ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 5⟩] .modify h31b.toP .fail ∧
    (∀ o, HandlePool.ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 5⟩] .modify h31b.toP o →
      o = .fail) ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (h31bo ++ [.resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 0⟩] .modify]) :=
  ⟨cfails (k := K0) (C := h31b) (o := .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 5⟩] .modify) (by decide),
    (HandlePool.pool_resolveMany_invalid_fails (k := K0) (L := h31b.toP) (j := 0)
      (pl := ⟨0, 4, 4, [⟨5, 0, true⟩, ⟨6, 0, true⟩]⟩) (hs := [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 5⟩])
      (m := .modify) (by decide) (by decide)).2,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `pool_newPool_written` (§72, §71, §67): the pool base with the entry 5 written before
`newPool`. -/
def pnwo : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 4, pt 4], .write 4 [5]]
/-- State reached by `pnwo` (§57). -/
def pnw : CState := cfinal K0 [] pnwo

/-- **pool_newPool_written** (handle-pool contract, class Lib; the draft witness
`pool_allocSlot_content_init`). `newPool` on a storage whose leaf 5 was written. Expected
(HandlePool v0.5, D.1: "`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage
d'entrée soient `Uninit`"): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; the other preconditions (those of
`newArena`, §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, and the guard of §56) hold. Twin without the write:
`newPool` and `allocSlot` are `ok`. -/
theorem pool_newPool_written : CRunsTo K0 [] pnwo pnw ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolStep pnw.othersP 4 4 pnw.toP .reject ∧
    NewArenaBase pnw.kern 4 4 ∧ Guard56 (HandlePool.liveInternals pnw.kern pnw.pools ::
      pnw.othersP) 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := pnw) (o := .newPool 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    by decide, crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State reached by `pb` (§57): a fresh pool, both slots free. -/
def pb0 : CState := cfinal K0 [] pb

/-- **pool_free_entry_handle** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). `freeSlot` of a free slot whose
identity and generation match the handle. Historical expected verdict: not `ok`, `fail` or `reject`
to arbitrate (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette
seule égalité"; the pool module read it as `fail`, HandlePool reading H-R2, a mismatch in form).
New expected verdict: `fail` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-6, arbitration Q12: "un handle d'entrée libre
est périmé : fail"; HP5-1'': `fail` on an invalid handle). Obtained: `fail`; `resolveMany` of the
same handle is `fail` too (HP5-5, HP5-6). Twin, the slot allocated first: `freeSlot` is `ok`. -/
theorem pool_free_entry_handle : CRunsTo K0 [] pb pb0 ∧
    HandlePool.FreeSlotStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ pb0.toP .fail ∧
    HandlePool.ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify pb0.toP .fail ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), cfails (k := K0) (C := pb0) (o := .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩) (by decide),
    cfails (k := K0) (C := pb0) (o := .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify) (by decide),

cfails (k := K0) (C := pb0) (o := .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify) (by decide),
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `pool_dead` (§69): slot 0 allocated (handle in 2), then `endUse` of the pool value 1,
which releases `internal` (§69 effect: the authorities held by the place end). -/
def pdo : List COp := pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .endUse 1]
/-- State reached by `pdo` (§57). -/
def pd : CState := cfinal K0 [] pdo

/-- **pool_dead** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). `allocSlot` and `freeSlot` on a pool whose
`internal` is no longer active; `internal` 4 is inactive while `MetaRight` (§36, `Modify` over the
pool value) still holds. `allocSlot`: expected (HandlePool v0.5, D.3: "`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige
un pool vivant") `reject`; obtained `reject`. `freeSlot`: historical expected verdict `reject`
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant**", a precondition checked
before the handle); new expected verdict `fail` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1'', arbitration Q5 extended
to `freeSlot`: "le handle d'un pool mort donne fail"); obtained `fail`. Twins without the `endUse`:
`allocSlot` and `freeSlot` are `ok`. -/
theorem pool_dead : CRunsTo K0 [] pdo pd ∧ ¬ pd.kern.Active 4 ∧
    MetaRight pd.kern ⟨4, 4, [], []⟩ ∧
    HandlePool.AllocSlotStep 0 3 pd.toP .reject ∧
    HandlePool.FreeSlotStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ pd.toP .fail ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .allocSlot 0 3]) ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    crejects (k := K0) (C := pd) (o := .allocSlot 0 3) (by decide),
    cfails (k := K0) (C := pd) (o := .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩) (by decide), crunsTo (by decide),
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Test contract of `pool_shared_right` (§68.1, §80): the pool value 1 is `SharedMutable`. -/
abbrev KSh : K := KD.toK { shared := [1] }

/-- Run of `pool_shared_right` (§60, §72, §68): slot 0 allocated; the caller passes 5, `Observe`
on the pool value, to a callee with the local 7, which updates the pool metadata by
`writeShared`. -/
def psro : List COp := pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .enter [5] [lf],
  .writeShared 5 [1]]
/-- State reached by `psro` (§57). -/
def psr : CState := cfinal KSh [] psro

/-- **pool_shared_right** (handle-pool contract, class Lib; the draft witness
`pool_freeSlot_shared_right`). A callee that may update the pool metadata only by `writeShared`
calls `allocSlot` and `freeSlot`. Expected (§36: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the
administering value, the `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient; this overrides the
`writeShared` right of material §4 and of HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): `reject`, `reject`.
Obtained: the `writeShared` is `ok` (§68), `allocSlot` and `freeSlot` are `reject` (`¬ MetaRight`;
the handle of `freeSlot` is valid, so the right decides, HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1''). Twin, the same
run with a `Modify` parameter on the pool value: `allocSlot` then `freeSlot` are `ok` (the
`freeSlot` under the `Modify` right). -/
theorem pool_shared_right : CRunsTo KSh [] psro psr ∧ ¬ MetaRight psr.kern ⟨4, 4, [], []⟩ ∧
    HandlePool.AllocSlotStep 0 7 psr.toP .reject ∧
    HandlePool.FreeSlotStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ psr.toP .reject ∧
    CRuns KSh [] (pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .derive 1 [1] .modify, .enter [5] [lf],
      .writeShared 5 [1], .allocSlot 0 7, .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), by decide, crejects (k := KSh) (C := psr) (o := .allocSlot 0 7) (by decide),
    crejects (k := KSh) (C := psr) (o := .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩) (by decide), crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Base of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` (§72, §71, §60, §65; HandlePool v0.5, D.1): frame 1 with
the allocator 0, the pool value 1 and the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 (entries 6, 7) owned by 1,
pool 0 on it with `internal` its root 5; then 6, `Modify` on the whole storage from 5, stored into
the leaf 4. -/
def pxo : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 5, pt 5], .newPool 5 5, .derive 5 [6, 7] .modify, .store 6 4]
/-- State reached by `pxo` (§57). -/
def px : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxo
/-- The twin of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` continued as the draft witness, up to its `freeSlot`:
pool 1 on `internal` 6 over the same storage; slot 0 allocated in each pool (the place 6 in both);
the leaf 6 written through 6. -/
def pxwo : List COp := pxo ++ [.newPool 5 6, .allocSlot 0 2, .allocSlot 1 3, .write 6 [6]]
/-- State reached by `pxwo` (§57). -/
def pxw : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxwo
/-- The same continuation without the write, then `freeSlot` of slot 0 of pool 1 (HandlePool
v0.5, HP5-1). -/
def pxto : List COp := pxo ++ [.newPool 5 6, .allocSlot 0 2, .allocSlot 1 3, .freeSlot 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩]
/-- State reached by `pxto` (§57). -/
def pxt : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxto

/-- **pool_two_freeSlot_cross** (handle-pool contract, class Lib). A second pool on the `internal`
5 of the live pool 0, over the same storage. Expected (§56; HandlePool v0.5, D.1: "Une autorité ne
peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes"): `reject` at the second `newPool`. Obtained:
`reject`; the other preconditions hold. Twin, the second pool on the distinct `internal` 6 (§56:
distinct identities over overlapping footprints are not forbidden): `ok`.

That twin continued as the draft witness: each pool allocates its slot 0, the place 6; the leaf 6
is written through 6; then `freeSlot` of slot 0 of pool 1. Historical verdict of this `freeSlot`:
`ok`, ending the content of the place 6, a live slot of pool 0 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the
`internal` 5 of pool 0, an ancestor of the `internal` 6 of pool 1, is exempt). New verdict:
`reject` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no leaf of the entry may be `Init`; the leaf 6 is `Init`).
Obtained: `reject`. Twin without the write: `ok`; the leaf 6 stays `Uninit` and the slot 0 of
pool 0 stays live at generation 0 (`freeSlot` has no kernel effect, HP5-1). On that state pool 0
cannot resolve its slot while the `internal` 6 of pool 1 is active: its own `internal` 5 has no
effective right on the storage (`reject`, §43 case 3). Twin of that `reject`: the same sequence
without the authority 6 (its `derive` and `store`) and the steps that use it (pool 1, its slot, its
`freeSlot`): `allocSlot` then `resolve` in pool 0, `ok`. Dropping only the steps of pool 1 does not
lift the `reject`: 6 is active from its `derive` on, before pool 1 exists. -/
theorem pool_two_freeSlot_cross : CRunsTo K0 [] pxo px ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolStep px.othersP 5 5 px.toP .reject ∧ NewArenaBase px.kern 5 5 ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint px.kern.P 5, px.kern.I l = .uninit) ∧
    CRunsTo K0 [] pxwo pxw ∧ pxw.kern.I 6 = .init ∧
    HandlePool.FreeSlotStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ pxw.toP .reject ∧
    CRunsTo K0 [] pxto pxt ∧ pxt.kern.I 6 = .uninit ∧
    pxt.pools = [⟨0, 5, 5, [⟨6, 0, true⟩, ⟨7, 0, false⟩]⟩,
      ⟨1, 5, 6, [⟨6, 1, false⟩, ⟨7, 0, false⟩]⟩] ∧
    HandlePool.ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify pxt.toP .reject ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (pxo.take 5 ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := px) (o := .newPool 5 5) (by decide), by decide,
    by decide, crunsTo (by decide), by decide,
    crejects (k := K0) (C := pxw) (o := .freeSlot 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩) (by decide),
    crunsTo (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    crejects (k := K0) (C := pxt) (o := .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify) (by decide),
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## The guard of §56 across registries -/

/-- Common base of the guard cases (§72, §71, §60, §65): frame 1 with the value 0 and the
allocator 1, written, the value 2 and the leaf 3; storage 4 (leaves 5, 6) allocated, owned by 0,
its root authority 4 held by 0; 5, `Modify` on the whole storage from 4, stored into the value 2.
Two candidate `internal` identities, 4 and 5, cover the storage. -/
def g0 : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .derive 4 [5, 6] .modify, .store 5 2]

/-- State after `g0` and `newPool 4 4` (§57). -/
def gp : CState := cfinal K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4])
/-- State after `g0` and `newArena 4 4` (§57). -/
def ga : CState := cfinal K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newArena 4 4])
/-- State after `g0` and `newStack 4 4` (§57). -/
def gs : CState := cfinal K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newStack 4 4])

/-- **pool_two_on_one_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib). A second pool on the `internal` 4 of a
live pool. Expected (§56: "An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live
administrative abstraction"; HandlePool v0.5, D.1): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; every
other precondition of `newPool` holds. Twin, a distinct `internal` (5) over the same storage:
`ok` (§56). -/
theorem pool_two_on_one_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4]) gp ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolStep gp.othersP 4 4 gp.toP .reject ∧ NewArenaBase gp.kern 4 4 ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint gp.kern.P 4, gp.kern.I l = .uninit) ∧
    Guard56 gp.othersP 4 ∧ CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4, .newPool 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := gp) (o := .newPool 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    by decide, by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **arena_on_pool_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib). An arena on the `internal` 4 of a live pool.
Expected (§56, §76.4: "no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library
instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity"): `reject`. Obtained:
`reject`; `NewArenaBase` holds and a guard over the arena registry alone would accept (§56:
"checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient"). Twin, `internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem arena_on_pool_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4]) gp ∧
    NewArenaStep gp.othersA 4 4 gp.toL .reject ∧ NewArenaPre gp.kern gp.arenas [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4, .newArena 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := gp) (o := .newArena 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **pool_on_arena_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib). A pool on the `internal` 4 of a live arena.
Expected (§56; HandlePool v0.5, D.1: the guard "sur les deux registres des abstractions
vivantes"): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; a guard over the pool registry alone would accept. Twin,
`internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem pool_on_arena_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newArena 4 4]) ga ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolStep ga.othersP 4 4 ga.toP .reject ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolPre ga.kern ga.pools [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newArena 4 4, .newPool 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := ga) (o := .newPool 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **stack_on_arena_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib; DS-v2). A stack on the `internal` 4 of a
live arena. Expected (§56): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; a guard over the stack registry alone
would accept. Twin, `internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem stack_on_arena_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newArena 4 4]) ga ∧
    DataStack.NewStackStep ga.othersD 4 4 ga.toD .reject ∧
    DataStack.NewStackPre ga.kern ga.stacks [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newArena 4 4, .newStack 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := ga) (o := .newStack 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **arena_on_stack_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib; DS-v2). An arena on the `internal` 4 of a
live stack. Expected (§56, §76.4): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; a guard over the arena registry
alone would accept. Twin, `internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem arena_on_stack_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newStack 4 4]) gs ∧
    NewArenaStep gs.othersA 4 4 gs.toL .reject ∧ NewArenaPre gs.kern gs.arenas [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newStack 4 4, .newArena 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := gs) (o := .newArena 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **stack_on_pool_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib; DS-v2). A stack on the `internal` 4 of a live
pool. Expected (§56): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; a guard over the stack registry alone would
accept. Twin, `internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem stack_on_pool_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4]) gp ∧
    DataStack.NewStackStep gp.othersD 4 4 gp.toD .reject ∧
    DataStack.NewStackPre gp.kern gp.stacks [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newPool 4 4, .newStack 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := gp) (o := .newStack 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **pool_on_stack_internal** (§56 guard, class Lib; DS-v2). A pool on the `internal` 4 of a live
stack. Expected (§56; HandlePool v0.5, D.1): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`; a guard over the
pool registry alone would accept. Twin, `internal` 5: `ok`. -/
theorem pool_on_stack_internal : CRunsTo K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newStack 4 4]) gs ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolStep gs.othersP 4 4 gs.toP .reject ∧
    HandlePool.NewPoolPre gs.kern gs.pools [] 4 4 ∧
    CRuns K0 [] (g0 ++ [.newStack 4 4, .newPool 4 5]) :=
  ⟨crunsTo (by decide), crejects (k := K0) (C := gs) (o := .newPool 4 4) (by decide), by decide,
    crunsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## Usage scenarios W1, W2 (material §5b) -/

/-- Run of W1 (§72, §71, §67, §63; HandlePool v0.5, D.1–D.3, HP5-1): frame 1 with the allocator
0, the pool value 1, the handle leaves 2 and 3, and two locals of the shape of a node, 4 (fields 5,
6, 7) and 8 (fields 9, 10, 11); storage 12 owned by the pool value, with the nodes 13 (fields
`data` 14, `parent` 15, `child` 16) and 17 (fields 18, 19, 20); pool on 12, its `internal` the
root authority 6 of the storage. The two nodes are linked both ways (the child of the first, the
parent of the second), each through a `resolve Modify`, writes and `unresolve`; then a resolution
of the first node to write its data. The value of the second node is then removed (arbitration
Q21, along the path of the Q3 witness): `resolve Modify` (companion 13, entry 14), write of its
last field not yet written (20), `transfer` of the entry to the local 4, `unresolve`. Last,
`freeSlot` of the second node, still designated by the child field of the first. -/
def w1o : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 4, pt 4, pt 4, lf, pt 8, pt 8, pt 8],
  .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 12, pt 13, pt 13, pt 13, pt 12, pt 17, pt 17, pt 17], .newPool 12 6,
  .allocSlot 0 2, .allocSlot 0 3,
  .resolve 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify, .write 8 [14, 16], .unresolve 7,

  .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 1, 0⟩]

the value of the second node not removed (§57). -/

/-- W1 continued by a resolution of the first node (companion 15, entry 16), the write of its

def w2o : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .write 2 [2], .write 3 [3],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 7, pt 8, pt 8, pt 7, pt 11, pt 11],

  .write 10 [9, 10], .read 12 [12, 13], .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 0⟩] .modify,

/-- Decidability of `ExercisableAt` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (s.ExercisableAt a m) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ exercisableAt_iff.symm

/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43): the current frame has an authority exercisable at `m` whose
effective mode permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def HasRight (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.ExercisableAt a m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s a l) m

/-- Decidability of `HasRight` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Decidable (HasRight s m q) := by
  unfold HasRight; infer_instance

/-- Authority `g` grounds the right `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43; §63.4, §69.2, §70.3: "the
exercisable authority on which that right rests"): it is exercisable at `m` and its effective mode
permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=
  g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m

/-- Decidability of `Grounds` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Decidable (Grounds s m q g) := by
  unfold Grounds; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` is the grounding authority `g` or belongs to its origin chain (§63.4, §69.2,
§70.3: "the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain"). -/
def RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g

/-- Decidability of `RightChain` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (RightChain s g j) := by
  unfold RightChain; infer_instance

/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/

/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
are accounted for transitively). -/
def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D

/-- The anchors of every place containing leaf `p` are valid, that is, active (§44; §66.3,
§67.3, §68.3). -/
def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- Decidability of `DepsValid` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- The frame of the effective anchor of `x` (the frame of its holder) exists and is `fd` or an
ancestor of `fd` (§44). -/
def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False

/-- Decidability of `EffAnchorOK` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance

/-- `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54): for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, the frame of the
effective anchor of `x` is the frame of `q` or an ancestor. -/
def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P` (decision procedure for §44). -/
theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩
to `corr(r)`; the anchors of `r` follow `corr(r)`. -/
def transferEff (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := s.P.map fun pl =>
      if heldIn s.P src pl.owner then { pl with owner := mvTo s.P src dst pl.owner } else pl
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init
      else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q src then [] else s.D q ++ movedTo s src dst q
    A := s.A.map fun y =>
      if heldIn s.P src y.holder then { y with holder := mvTo s.P src dst y.holder } else y }

/-- Active derived authority covering a leaf of `src` and not held within it (§63.4). -/
def ActiveDerivedOutside (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P src y.holder ∧
    ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P src) False

/-- Decidability of `ActiveDerivedOutside` (§63.4). -/
instance (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Decidable (ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) := by
  unfold ActiveDerivedOutside; infer_instance

/-- The holder moves with the value at `src` (§63.6, §63.7): a part of `src` or storage it owns,
transitively. -/
def HolderMoves (s : S3) (src : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place p => partOf s.P p src ∨ OwnedIn s.P src p
  | .frame _ => False

/-- Decidability of `HolderMoves` (§63.7). -/
instance (s : S3) (src : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderMoves s src h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold HolderMoves <;> infer_instance

/-- Authority `x` is a moved held authority (§63.7): its holder moves with the value at `src`. -/
def AnchorMoves (s : S3) (src x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => HolderMoves s src y.holder) False

/-- Decidability of `AnchorMoves` (§63.7). -/
instance (s : S3) (src x : Nat) : Decidable (AnchorMoves s src x) := by
  unfold AnchorMoves; infer_instance

/-- Dependencies of the usable places following the value at `src` (§63.6): the anchors of its
parts and of the usable storage it owns, transitively. -/
def movedDeps (s : S3) (src : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun q =>
    decide (partOf s.P q src ∨ (OwnedIn s.P src q ∧ s.Usable q))).flatMap s.D

/-- Leaves of a holder (§63.8): those of a place, none for a frame. -/
def holderLeaves (s : S3) : Holder → List Nat
  | .place p => footprint s.P p
  | .frame _ => []

/-- Authority `a` is active and covers a leaf of its own holder (§63.8). -/
def SelfLock (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder) False

/-- Decidability of `SelfLock` (§63.8). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (SelfLock s a) := by unfold SelfLock; infer_instance

/-- Local self-blocking prevention (§63.8): no authority held before the step within `src` covers,
in the resulting state, a leaf of its new holder `corr(r)`. -/
def NoLocalSelfLock (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => heldIn s.P src y.holder) False →
    ¬ SelfLock (transferEff s src dst) j

/-- Decidability of `NoLocalSelfLock` (§63.8). -/
instance (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (NoLocalSelfLock s src dst) := by
  unfold NoLocalSelfLock; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `transfer` (§63). -/
structure TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §63.1: `source` is usable. -/
  srcUsable : s.Usable src
  /-- §63.1: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the source. -/
  srcRight : HasRight s .modify src
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the destination. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- §63.2: same shape of ordered subtrees. -/
  sameShape : SameShape s.P src dst
  /-- §63.3: all source leaves are `Init`. -/
  srcInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init
  /-- §63.3: no destination leaf is `Init`. -/

import Ern.Corpus.Runner
import Ern.Lib.DataStack

/-!
# Corpus DataStack: the stack library (test module)

Cases of the library instance `DataStack` of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`, run on
the reference kernel (§60–§75) through the library of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. The spec does not define
the contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"); the contract is DS-v2, non-normative, stated in the
module docstring of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. This is a test module: no model or library module imports
it.

* `DOp`: a kernel operation O1–O16 of the corpus runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`), or a stack
  operation `newStack`, `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow` (DS-v2).
* `dstep k D o`: the computed outcome (§58); `dstep_sound`: it is an outcome of the relation of the
  operation (`DOpRel`: the kernel relation with the stack metadata unchanged, `NewStackStep`,
  `PushStep`, `MarkStep`, `RewindStep`, `GrowStep`), `ok`, `reject` and `fail` alike.
* `druns`: a run from `DState.init statics` (§47) whose steps are all `ok` reaches a state that is
  library-reachable (`DReach`) and whose kernel state is reachable by O1–O16 (§57,
  `DReach.reachable`).
* `newStack` consults the stack registry and no other (§56, `others = []`): the library states of
  these runs hold no administration other than stacks.

Each case states the reached state with `DRunsTo`, the verdict of the step under test with the
relation of its operation on that state (decided by `decide`; `rewind_dead_fails` adds that `fail`
is the only outcome), and its positive twin (the same sequence without the faulty element,
accepted). Its docstring gives the expected verdict from its source (the stack contract of the
brief, DS-v1, whose text DS-v2 keeps and the cases quote as DS-v2; the brief's ABA and multi-stack
frame scenarios; the draft DataStack cases of the derivability material, non-normative, which settle
no verdict alone), the obtained verdict, the class (`Lib`: library instance) and the twin. The
source material is no longer available: each source verdict is the one recorded by the spec v0
edition of this module and by the corpus map of the reconstruction. Where DS-v2 changes the verdict
a source gave, the docstring records the historical expected verdict, its justification, the new
expected verdict, derived from the text of the deciding DS-v2 item, and that item: the third `grow`
of DS03 and DS05, both "to arbitrate" under DS-v1. A case whose obtained verdict differs from the
expected one would be kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH**; none does.

DS-v2 items on which a verdict or arrival state depends: DS2-1 at every `mark` (`AdminRight` holds
on the stack of each); DS2-2 at every `grow` (the block of each is held by its recorded destination:
no block value is transferred); DS2-4 at every `rewind` (no cell at a position `≥` the current top
is covered, so the cells that decide are those between the top of the mark and the top, as in the
spec v0 edition of this module); the dead or foreign mark `fail` before the right (DS02, DS06,
DS08); `push` without room `fail` (DS05); `grow` of a `b` that is no block `reject` (DS03); §76.5
and §76.6 at every `newStack`. DS2-3 (a dead stack), DS2-5 (`grow` with `extra = 0`) and DS2-6
(`rewind` on a missing stack) occur in no case here; their examples are in `Ern.Lib.DataStack`
(`Witness.dead_stack_marks_fail`, `Witness.grow_zero_reissues`,
`Witness.rewind_missing_stack_fails`).

Not encoded: the draft `case_rewind_reading` (its reading of "above the mark" is decided by DS2-4,
example `Witness.rewind_rejects_above_top` of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`, under which its `rewind` with a
covered cell above the current top is `reject`); the draft `case_static_before_fail` other than its
`push` without room (its `Init`-destination conjuncts are changed by §77.2); the kernel `newArena`
conjuncts of the draft `case_stacks` (the stack-library state holds no arena registry; the
cross-registry cases of §56 are another module).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus Ern.Lib.DataStack

/-! ## Test contract and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

/-- A leaf part of the shape element `p` (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev pt (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat := (some p, 0)

/-- One stack (DS-v2, §72, §60, §65, §76 read for a stack): frame 1 with the stack value 0, the
storage 1 with the cells 2, 3, 4, and the destinations 5, 6, 7 (root authorities 0 on 0, 1 on 1,
2 on 5, 3 on 6, 4 on 7); `internal` 5, `Modify` derived from the root of the storage on its cells,
stored into the stack value; stack 0 created on 1 with `internal` 5. -/
def setup1 : List DOp :=
  [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, pt 1, pt 1, pt 1, lf, lf, lf]),
    .kernel (.derive 1 [2, 3, 4] .modify), .kernel (.store 5 0), .newStack 1 5]

/-! ## One stack: `rewind`, marks, `grow`, `push` (DS-v2) -/

/-- Run of DS01 (DS-v2): mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`; `push` of 2 cells into 5 (block 6 on `[2, 3]`); mark
`⟨0, 1, 2⟩`; `push` of 1 cell into 6 (block 7 on `[4]`). -/
def ds01o : List DOp := setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 2 5, .mark 0, .push 0 1 6]
/-- State reached by `ds01o` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds01 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds01o

/-- **DS01** (draft `case_rewind`; DS-v2 "rewind m … rejects if an active authority derived from
internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every
mark above it", with DS2-4: a cell above m is a cell at a position `≥ m.top`; class Lib).
`rewind ⟨0, 1, 2⟩` while block 7, active and derived from `internal` 5, covers cell 4, at position
2, above the mark; then after the program releases 7. Expected (DS-v2, draft):
`reject`, then `ok` with top 2, block 6 kept, mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` kept. Obtained: `reject` (`split` of
`internal` on `[4]` rejected, §43 case 3, §61.1), then `ok` with that metadata (§62, §61). Twins:
the same sequence without the second `push`, `ok`; and the run with `release(7)` before the
`rewind`, `ok`. -/
theorem DS01 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds01o ds01 ∧
    ds01.kern.A[7]? = some ⟨.modify, some 5, [4], .place 6, true⟩ ∧
    RewindStep K0 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩ ds01 .reject ∧
    DRuns K0 [] (setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 2 5, .mark 0, .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩]) ∧
    DRuns K0 [] (ds01o ++ [.kernel (.release 7), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩]) ∧
    (dfinal K0 [] (ds01o ++ [.kernel (.release 7), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩])).stacks =
      [⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 2, [⟨0, 2, 6, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]⟩] :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), by decide, drejects (k := K0) (o := .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩) (by decide),
    druns (by decide), druns (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- Run of DS02 (DS-v2): the run of DS01, `release(7)`, `rewind ⟨0, 1, 2⟩` (top back to 2), then a
new mark at the same top: `⟨0, 2, 2⟩`. -/
def ds02o : List DOp := ds01o ++ [.kernel (.release 7), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩, .mark 0]
/-- State reached by `ds02o` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds02 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds02o

/-- **DS02** (draft `case_aba`; DS-v2 "Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
"rewind m fails on a dead … mark"; class Lib). ABA: the top is back at 2, the top of the removed
mark `⟨0, 1, 2⟩`, and a new mark `⟨0, 2, 2⟩` is live there. Expected (DS-v2, draft): `rewind` of the
removed mark `fail`, of the new mark `ok`. Obtained: `fail`, with no other outcome (§58;
`rewind_dead_fails`), and `ok`. Twin of the `fail`: `rewind` of the new mark at the same position,
`ok`. -/
theorem DS02 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds02o ds02 ∧
    ds02.stacks = [⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 2, [⟨0, 2, 6, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 2⟩]⟩] ∧
    (RewindStep K0 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩ ds02 .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep K0 0 ⟨0, 1, 2⟩ ds02 o → o = .fail) ∧
    DRuns K0 [] (ds02o ++ [.rewind 0 ⟨0, 2, 2⟩]) :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), by decide,
    rewind_dead_fails (st := ⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 2, [⟨0, 2, 6, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 2⟩]⟩)
      (by decide) (by decide),
    druns (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of DS03 (DS-v2): the run of DS02, then `grow` of block 6 (`[2, 3]`, at the top) by one
cell. -/
def ds03o : List DOp := ds02o ++ [.grow 0 6 1]
/-- State reached by `ds03o` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds03 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds03o

/-- **DS03** (draft `case_grow`; DS-v2 "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space
directly after the block, fail otherwise)", DS2-2 "grow stores the new block authority into the
place that currently holds the block authority b", and "grow of a b that is no block of the stack
is reject"; class Lib). `grow(6, 1)` with one cell after the block; then `grow(9, 1)` with no cell
left; then `grow(6, 1)` of the replaced block.
Expected: `ok` (DS-v2: block `⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩` of the same base, authority 9 on `[2, 3, 4]`, stored
into place 5, which holds block 6: no block value is transferred, so it is also the recorded
destination), then `fail` (DS-v2 "fail otherwise": no cell follows the block).
For the replaced block, the verdict changes with DS-v2. Historical expected verdict (DS-v1): none,
to arbitrate. Justification: DS-v1 says nothing of a `b` that is no block of the stack (the
`reject` of the draft `case_grow` is module behaviour, not a source), and the v0 edition of this
case marked it **MISMATCH** in form against the obtained `reject`. New expected verdict: `reject`,
decided by the DS-v2 item "`grow` of a `b` that is no block of the stack is `reject`" (Q11 (b),
DS-R5): 6 is no block of the stack after the first `grow`.
Obtained: `ok` (`release`, `split`, `store` into the holder 5, §62, §61, §65) with that block and
footprint; `fail` (no room, availability §77.4); `reject` (6 is no block of the stack). Twin of the
`fail` and of the `reject`: `grow(6, 1)` with one cell after the block, the `ok` step of this run.
-/
theorem DS03 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds03o ds03 ∧
    ds03.stacks = [⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 3, [⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 2⟩]⟩] ∧
    ds03.kern.afp 9 = [2, 3, 4] ∧
    GrowStep K0 0 9 1 ds03 .fail ∧ GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), by decide, by decide, dfails (k := K0) (o := .grow 0 9 1) (by decide),
    drejects (k := K0) (o := .grow 0 6 1) (by decide)⟩

/-- **DS04** (DS-v2 "grow is in place only (…, extension into the space directly after the block,
fail otherwise)"; class Lib). In the state of DS01, `grow(6, 1)` of block 6 (`[2, 3]`), live but not
the last one: block 7 occupies cell 4 after it. Expected (DS-v2, "fail otherwise"; DS2-5 does not
apply, `extra` is 1): `fail` (the draft's `grow`, which handled the last block only, rejected).
Obtained: `fail` (release of 6, the holder 5 of 6 found, DS2-2, static checks, then `InPlace`
fails, §77.4). Twin: the same sequence without the second `push`, `ok`. -/
theorem DS04 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds01o ds01 ∧ GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds01 .fail ∧
    DRuns K0 [] (setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 2 5, .mark 0, .grow 0 6 1]) :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), dfails (k := K0) (o := .grow 0 6 1) (by decide), druns (by decide)⟩

/-- State reached by `setup1` (§57; DS-v2): stack 0 with 3 cells, top 0. -/
def ds05 : DState := dfinal K0 [] setup1

/-- **DS05** (draft `case_static_before_fail`, `push 0 4 5`; DS-v2 "push and grow use the derived
issue" and "push without room is fail"; class Lib). `push` of 4 cells into 5 on a stack of 3 cells.
The verdict changes with DS-v2. Historical expected verdict (DS-v1): none, to arbitrate.
Justification: DS-v1 does not settle a `push` without room; the reading DS-R7 gave `fail`
(availability, §77.4), its recorded alternative `reject` ("region belongs to the administered
storage", §77.2, static), and the v0 edition of this case marked it **MISMATCH** in form against

/-- Run of DS06 (DS-v2): mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`, `push` of one cell into 5 (block 6), mark `⟨0, 1, 1⟩`,
`release(6)`, `rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩`. -/
def ds06o : List DOp :=
  setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 1 5, .mark 0, .kernel (.release 6), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩]
/-- State reached by `ds06o` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds06 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds06o

/-- **DS06** (DS-v2, brief obligation 6: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark" and "removes
m and every mark above it"; class Lib). `rewind ⟨0, 1, 1⟩` after `rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩`
removed it as a later mark. Expected (DS-v2): `fail`. Obtained: `fail`, with no other outcome (§58;
`rewind_dead_fails`); both marks are gone. Twin: the same sequence without `rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩`:
`rewind ⟨0, 1, 1⟩`, `ok`. -/
theorem DS06 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds06o ds06 ∧ ds06.stacks = [⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 0, [], []⟩] ∧
    (RewindStep K0 0 ⟨0, 1, 1⟩ ds06 .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep K0 0 ⟨0, 1, 1⟩ ds06 o → o = .fail) ∧
    DRuns K0 [] (setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 1 5, .mark 0, .kernel (.release 6),
      .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 1⟩]) :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), by decide,
    rewind_dead_fails (st := ⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 0, [], []⟩) (by decide) (by decide),
    druns (by decide)⟩

/-! ## Several stacks (DS-v2; §56) -/

/-- Two stacks (DS-v2, §72, §60, §65, §76 read for a stack): frame 1 with the stack values 0 and 8,
the storages 1 (cells 2, 3, 4) and 9 (cells 10, 11), the destinations 5, 6, 7, 12 (root
authorities 0 on 0, 1 on 1, 2 on 5, 3 on 6, 4 on 7, 5 on 8, 6 on 9, 7 on 12); `internal` 8 on the
cells of 1, stored into 0, stack 0; `internal` 9 on the cells of 9, stored into 8, stack 1. -/
def setup2 : List DOp :=
  [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, pt 1, pt 1, pt 1, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 9, pt 9, lf]),
    .kernel (.derive 1 [2, 3, 4] .modify), .kernel (.store 8 0), .newStack 1 8,
    .kernel (.derive 6 [10, 11] .modify), .kernel (.store 9 8), .newStack 9 9]
/-- State reached by `setup2` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds07 : DState := dfinal K0 [] setup2

/-- **DS07** (draft `case_stacks`, first part; §56 "An authority identity may serve as `internal`
for at most one live administrative abstraction"; class Lib). A second `newStack` with `internal`
8, already the `internal` of the live stack 0. Expected (§56, draft): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`
by the guard of §56 alone: the other preconditions (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3, §76.5 and §76.6
read for a stack) hold. Twin: the same sequence without the first registration of 8, `ok`. The
draft's conjuncts on a kernel `newArena` have no counterpart here: the stack-library state holds no
arena registry (cross-registry cases of §56 belong to another module). -/
theorem DS07 : DRunsTo K0 [] setup2 ds07 ∧ NewStackStep [] 1 8 ds07 .reject ∧
    NewArenaBase ds07.kern 1 8 ∧ ¬ Guard56 [stackInternals ds07.kern ds07.stacks] 8 ∧
    DRuns K0 [] [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, pt 1, pt 1, pt 1, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 9, pt 9,
      lf]), .kernel (.derive 1 [2, 3, 4] .modify), .kernel (.store 8 0),
      .kernel (.derive 6 [10, 11] .modify), .kernel (.store 9 8), .newStack 9 9, .newStack 1 8] :=
  ⟨druns (by decide), drejects (k := K0) (o := .newStack 1 8) (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    druns (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of DS08 (DS-v2): on the two stacks, mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`; `push` of one cell of stack 0 into 5
(block 10 on `[2]`); `push` of one cell of stack 1 into 12 (block 11 on `[10]`); mark
`⟨1, 1, 1⟩`. -/
def ds08o : List DOp := setup2 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 1 5, .push 1 1 12, .mark 1]
/-- State reached by `ds08o` (§57; DS-v2). -/
def ds08 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds08o

/-- **DS08** (draft `case_stacks`, second part; DS-v2, brief obligation 6: "Marks carry stack
identity"; "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark"; class Lib). Each stack
has its own top, blocks and marks. `rewind ⟨0, 0, 0⟩` of stack 0 while block 10 lives; `rewind` of
stack 0 to the mark `⟨1, 1, 1⟩` of stack 1; `rewind` of stack 1 to its mark, then a new `push` on
it. Expected (draft, DS-v2): `reject`, `fail`, `ok`. Obtained: `reject` (§43 case 3, §61.1),
`fail` with no other outcome (§58; `rewind_dead_fails`), `ok`. Twins: after `release(10)`,

    ds08.stacks = [⟨1, 8, [2, 3, 4], 1, [⟨0, 1, 10, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]⟩,
      ⟨9, 9, [10, 11], 1, [⟨0, 1, 11, 12⟩], [⟨1, 1, 1⟩]⟩] ∧

  ⟨druns (by decide), by decide, drejects (k := K0) (o := .rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩) (by decide),
    druns (by decide),
    rewind_dead_fails (st := ⟨1, 8, [2, 3, 4], 1, [⟨0, 1, 10, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]⟩) (by decide)
      (by decide),
    druns (by decide)⟩

/-- Entry of DS09 (§72, §60; DS-v2): on the two stacks, the caller pushes one cell of stack 0 into

theorem DS09 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds09o ds09 ∧
